context.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present authorizations for a mid-size payment processor in AWS (eu-west-1). Its core purpose is to score 3,000 TPS under 50 ms P99 latency, manage fraud analyst reviews, and ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance with 7-year tamper-evident auditability.]

## Key Elements
* **End Customer:** Cardholder initiating transactions
* **Payment Gateway:** External client submitting payment authorizations via HTTPS
* **API Gateway & AWS WAF:** Ingress management enforcing TLS 1.3, rate-limiting, and velocity-based risk throttling
* **Scoring Engine:** Stateless microservice container running on AWS ECS/Fargate for real-time fraud evaluation
* **Case Management UI:** Internal web application for fraud analysts using OIDC/OAuth2 and hardware-backed MFA
* **Audit & Storage Layer:** Amazon S3 with Object Lock (Compliance Mode) and KMS-envelope encryption for 7-year retention

## Relationships
* **Payment Gateway to API Gateway:** Submits authorization requests via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
* **API Gateway to Scoring Engine:** Forwards payload for real-time evaluation via mTLS
* **Scoring Engine to Audit & Storage Layer:** Writes tamper-evident decisions, model versions, and inputs via AWS SDK
* **Fraud Analyst to Case Management UI:** Reviews suspicious payments via HTTPS without accessing raw PAN data

## Technology Stack
* **AWS ECS/Fargate:** Container orchestration for stateless scoring microservices, avoiding serverless cold starts to maintain <50ms P99 latency
* **Amazon S3 with Object Lock:** Provides tamper-evident, cost-optimized 7-year audit log retention using compliance mode and lifecycle tiering
* **AWS API Gateway & AWS WAF:** Handles fail-open circuit breakers, rate-limiting, and velocity-based throttling during outages
* **AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) Private CA:** Secures internal microservice communication using mutual TLS (mTLS)

## Rationale
[This architecture meets strict performance and compliance demands using fully managed AWS services to fit the €25,000/month budget and operational limits of a 3-person engineering team. It enforces PCI-DSS boundaries, secure tokenization, and fail-open resilience while preserving tamper-evident 7-year auditability.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening platform evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud to protect revenue while enabling manual case review. It is engineered for a mid-size payment processor to meet strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability.]

## Key Elements
* **Users:** Cardholder, Fraud Analyst, Risk/Fraud Operations Manager
* **External Systems:** Payment Gateway
* **Containers:** API Gateway, Scoring Engine Container, Case Management Container, Redis Cache, S3 Glacier Object Lock Storage
* **Technologies:** AWS ECS (Fargate), AWS ElastiCache Serverless, AWS S3 Glacier with Object Lock, AWS KMS, AWS Cognito

## Relationships
* **Payment Gateway to API Gateway:** Sends payment authorization requests via HTTPS using mTLS and TLS 1.3.
* **API Gateway to Scoring Engine Container:** Routes scoring requests over internal VPC networking.
* **Scoring Engine Container to Redis Cache:** Queries cached fallback ruleset over isolated VPC subnet during outages (R-07).
* **Scoring Engine Container to S3 Glacier:** Writes cryptographically signed audit logs using AWS KMS envelope encryption.
* **Fraud Analyst / Manager to Case Management Container:** Accesses review UI and operational metrics via OAuth2/OIDC and AWS Cognito authentication.

## Technology Stack
* **AWS ECS (Fargate):** Selected for container orchestration to ensure zero-downtime rolling updates (R-03) with minimal operational overhead for a 3-person team.
* **AWS ElastiCache Serverless:** Powers the Redis degraded-mode fallback cache to support R-07 without manual cluster management.
* **AWS S3 Glacier with Object Lock:** Implements tamper-evident storage for 7-year audit logs (R-06) within budget limits.
* **AWS KMS:** Provides envelope encryption for cryptographic signing of decision audit logs.
* **AWS Cognito:** Manages user authentication and role-based access control (RBAC) for analysts and managers.

## Rationale
[The serverless-managed AWS architecture minimizes operational burden for a three-engineer team while strictly enforcing budget and compliance constraints. Decoupled tokenized boundaries and isolated audit logging ensure PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.]

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations in real-time to prevent fraud while ensuring strict PCI-DSS compliance. It provides low-latency fraud scoring and an analyst case management interface within a fixed budget of €25,000 per month.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway (External System)
- Fraud Analyst (Person)
- API Gateway (AWS API Gateway HTTP API with AWS WAF)
- Scoring Engine Container (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Container (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Cache & Storage (AWS ElastiCache Redis, AWS S3 Glacier with Object Lock, AWS KMS)
- Security & IAM (AWS Cognito, AWS IAM, AWS X-Ray)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> API Gateway: Sends payment authorization requests [HTTPS, mTLS, TLS 1.3]
- API Gateway -> Scoring Engine Container: Routes scoring requests [Internal VPC Networking, AWS VPC Security Groups]
- API Gateway -> Case Management Container: Routes analyst review requests [HTTPS, JWT validation, AWS Cognito]
- Scoring Engine Container -> AWS ElastiCache Redis: Retrieves rule caches and rate-limiting counters [Internal VPC]
- System Containers -> AWS S3 Glacier: Stores tamper-evident audit logs and decisions [AWS KMS, Object Lock]

## Technology Stack
- Ingress: AWS API Gateway (HTTP API) chosen for native auto-scaling and low operational overhead for a 3-engineer team.
- Compute: AWS ECS (Fargate) selected for containerized workloads to eliminate server management.
- Security & Compliance: AWS WAF and AWS KMS chosen for PCI-DSS Level 1 tokenization, rate limiting, and data encryption.
- Caching: AWS ElastiCache (Redis) utilized for distributed rate limiting and low-latency feature lookups.
- Audit & Storage: AWS S3 Glacier with Object Lock configured to meet the 7-year tamper-evident audit requirement.

## Rationale
This architecture uses fully managed AWS serverless and container services to meet strict performance (<50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS) and compliance (PCI-DSS Level 1) requirements within a fixed €25,000 monthly budget. Offloading infrastructure management to managed services enables a three-engineer team to operate the platform reliably with zero downtime.

Scoring Engine Container.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening is a low-latency platform designed to evaluate card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manage suspicious cases. It ensures secure, auditable, and sub-50ms transaction processing within strict budgetary and compliance constraints.

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analyst (Internal User)
* Cardholder / End Customer (External User)
* API Gateway (AWS ECS Fargate)
* Scoring Engine Container (AWS ECS Fargate)
* Case Management Container (AWS ECS Fargate, AWS Cognito)
* Redis Cache (AWS ElastiCache Serverless)
* S3 Glacier Object Lock Storage (AWS S3 Glacier with Object Lock, AWS KMS)

## Relationships
* API Gateway -> Scoring Engine Container: Routes real-time scoring requests via internal VPC networking / mTLS
* Scoring Engine Container -> Redis Cache: Queries cached fallback ruleset during outages via isolated VPC subnet
* Scoring Engine Container -> S3 Glacier Object Lock Storage: Writes cryptographically signed audit logs via AWS KMS envelope encryption

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS (Fargate): Container orchestration chosen for predictable sizing and minimal operational overhead for a 3-engineer team.
* AWS ElastiCache Serverless (Redis): Provides sub-millisecond fallback rule caching to meet the 50ms P99 latency SLA.
* AWS S3 Glacier with Object Lock & AWS KMS: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year compliant audit logging meeting PCI-DSS Level 1 standards.
* Amazon CloudWatch & ECS Container Insights: Native metrics and structured JSON logging used to eliminate expensive APM licensing and respect the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Rationale
The architecture utilizes serverless and managed AWS services to maintain high availability and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance without exceeding the 25,000 EUR monthly budget or requiring a large operations team. Strict cryptographic controls, local circuit breakers, and container security guardrails ensure real-time performance and immutable auditability.

Case Management Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management Container provides a secure review interface and API backend for fraud analysts and managers to investigate suspicious transactions. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while maintaining immutable audit trails and SLA-driven case queues.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (Person)
- Risk/Fraud Operations Manager (Person)
- API Gateway (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Container (AWS ECS Fargate)
- AWS Cognito
- Amazon ElastiCache Serverless (Redis)
- Amazon CloudWatch
- AWS S3 Glacier with Object Lock

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst -> API Gateway: Accesses review UI and submits decisions [HTTPS, OAuth2/OIDC, AWS Cognito]
- Risk/Fraud Operations Manager -> API Gateway: Accesses operational metrics and queues [HTTPS, OAuth2/OIDC, AWS Cognito]
- API Gateway -> Case Management Container: Forwards authenticated review requests [mTLS / AWS IAM SigV4, HTTPS]
- Case Management Container -> Amazon ElastiCache Serverless: Caches session state and queue data [Redis Protocol, TLS 1.3, AWS KMS]
- Case Management Container -> AWS S3 Glacier: Stores tamper-evident audit logs and decisions [HTTPS, AWS KMS, Object Lock]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate (Spot): Runs containerized backend workloads efficiently within the budget.
- AWS Cognito: Manages authentication, short-lived JWTs (15 min), and RBAC segregation.
- Amazon ElastiCache Serverless (Redis): Caches session data with encryption at rest via AWS KMS.
- Amazon CloudWatch: Monitors container insights and metrics with automated log scrubbing.
- AWS S3 Glacier with Object Lock: Enforces tamper-evident 7-year audit retention (R-06).

## Rationale
This architecture balances strict PCI-DSS Level 1 security controls and 7-year auditability with the operational constraints of a three-engineer team. Serverless and managed AWS services minimize operational overhead while fitting within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

  - type: "component"

    description: "Generates and sends immutable audit trails and tamper-evident decision logs to storage."

    description: "Manages SLA-driven case queues and state synchronization."

    description: "Updates and retrieves case queue data"
  - source: "Review Interface Controller"
    destination: "Audit Logger"
    description: "Dispatches review decisions for immutable logging"

Redis Cache.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at 3,000 TPS while enabling analyst case reviews. It ensures strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget operated by three engineers.

## Key Elements
- Cardholders and Fraud Analysts (Users)
- Payment Gateway (External System)
- API Gateway (AWS ECS Fargate Container)
- Scoring Engine Container (AWS ECS Fargate Container)
- Case Management Container (AWS ECS Fargate Container, AWS Cognito)
- Amazon ElastiCache Redis OSS Multi-AZ Cluster (`cache.m6g.large`)
- S3 Glacier Object Lock Storage (AWS S3 Glacier, AWS KMS)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> API Gateway: Forwards payment authorizations via HTTPS/TLS 1.3
- API Gateway -> Scoring Engine Container: Routes authorization payloads via internal gRPC
- Scoring Engine Container -> Amazon ElastiCache Redis Cluster: Queries fallback ruleset via Redis OSS protocol with TLS in transit
- Scoring Engine Container -> S3 Glacier Object Lock Storage: Persists immutable decision audit logs via AWS SDK / KMS

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS (Fargate): Container orchestration minimizing operational overhead for a three-person team
- Amazon ElastiCache Redis OSS (`cache.m6g.large`): Provisioned multi-AZ caching ensuring deterministic sub-50ms latency and budget control
- AWS KMS & AWS Secrets Manager: Enforces encryption at rest (AES-256) and dynamic secret injection for PCI-DSS compliance
- AWS S3 Glacier with Object Lock: Provides tamper-evident 7-year audit retention

## Rationale
This architecture uses provisioned AWS managed services to guarantee predictable costs and deterministic sub-50ms P99 latency. Multi-AZ redundancy and a Redis fallback cache secure high availability and uptime requirements.

S3 Glacier Object Lock Storage.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at 3,000 requests per second and manages suspicious cases. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability on AWS.

## Key Elements
- Scoring Engine Container (AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Case Management Container (AWS ECS on Fargate, AWS Cognito)
- API Gateway (AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Redis Cache (AWS ElastiCache Serverless)
- S3 Glacier Object Lock Storage (AWS S3 Glacier Flexible Archive with Object Lock, AWS KMS)
- Amazon Kinesis Firehose (Managed batching)
- Fraud Analyst (User)
- Payment Gateway (External System)

## Relationships
- Scoring Engine Container -> S3 Glacier Object Lock Storage: Writes cryptographically signed audit logs via Amazon Kinesis Firehose [TLS 1.3, AWS KMS]
- Fraud Analyst -> Case Management Container: Reviews suspicious payments [HTTPS]
- API Gateway -> Scoring Engine Container: Routes authorization requests [gRPC / REST]
- Scoring Engine Container -> Redis Cache: Retrieves rules and session data [Redis Protocol]

## Technology Stack
- Compute: AWS ECS with AWS Fargate for zero-server management by a 3-engineer team
- Storage & Audit: AWS S3 Glacier Flexible Archive with Object Lock (COMPLIANCE mode) and AWS KMS for 7-year tamper-evident retention
- Ingestion & Batching: Amazon Kinesis Firehose to batch high-frequency logs and reduce API costs
- Caching: AWS ElastiCache Serverless for low-latency rule and session lookups
- Authentication: AWS Cognito for secure analyst access management

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to maintain ultra-low operational overhead suitable for a three-engineer team. Strict encryption, WORM storage, and batching satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year audit requirements within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

scope: "Component diagram for the S3 Glacier Object Lock Storage container"

  name: "S3 Glacier Object Lock Storage"

    description: "Manages WORM storage, cryptographic signing, and 7-year tamper-evident retention for audit logs."
  - type: "component"
    name: "Firehose Ingestion Handler"
    technology: "Amazon Kinesis Firehose"
    description: "Batches high-frequency logs from the Scoring Engine Container before writing to storage to reduce API costs."

  - source: "Firehose Ingestion Handler"
    destination: "Object Lock Manager"
    description: "Writes cryptographically signed audit logs [TLS 1.3, AWS KMS]"
